title: Motional Kerr-Cat States of an Atom in an Optical Tweezer
authors: Steven K. Pampel, Gur Lubin, Dawson P. Hewatt, Conall McCabe, Jaeyong Hwang, Sean R. Muleady, Tianrui Xu, Ana Maria Rey, Cindy A. Regal
abstract: Schrödinger cat states - quantum superpositions of classically or macroscopically distinct states - constitute a powerful resource for quantum computing, enhanced metrology, and probing coherence on large scales. Encoding such states in the phase space of an oscillator requires a nonlinearity, typically inherited from an auxiliary degree of freedom such as atomic spin or a Josephson junction. Neutral atoms trapped in reconfigurable optical tweezer arrays - a leading platform for quantum science and computing - provide an intrinsic nonlinearity via the motion of a single atom in a tightly focused trap. However, this self-Kerr mechanism has not previously been exploited for cat-state generation, and remains largely unexplored as a resource for motional-state control. Here we realize Schrödinger cat states in the quantized motion of a single neutral atom trapped in an optical tweezer. By modulating the depth and position, we demonstrate parity control of both Kerr-cat and Fock states alongside tunable nonlinearity, establishing a spin- and species-independent framework for controlling motion. We further show that the cat-state encoding is intrinsically robust against trap-frequency fluctuations that otherwise limit the fidelity of direct Fock-state transitions. These results establish Kerr-based control of neutral-atom motion as a new paradigm for cat-state and bosonic-state engineering in optical tweezers, providing a route toward quantum-error-correcting codes such as grid states, and toward quantum-enhanced sensing with arrays of non-Gaussian states.
summary: The research demonstrates the creation and control of Schrödinger cat states in the quantized motion of an atom trapped by an optical tweezer. They exploit the intrinsic Kerr nonlinearity of the trap potential, establishing a novel method for non-Gaussian state engineering. This work is significant because it provides a robust platform for generating complex quantum resources needed for advanced quantum computing applications.
main_problem: The primary goal is realizing and controlling Schrödinger cat states using the motional degrees of freedom of a single neutral atom trapped in an optical tweezer.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated the generation and parity control of Kerr-cat and Fock states, establishing a new paradigm for non-Gaussian state engineering in optical tweezers.
method: State preparation involves adiabatically modulating trap depth and position (painting) to tune the intrinsic self-Kerr nonlinearity, followed by time-of-flight quantum-state tomography for measurement.
model_or_system: The system is a neutral atom trapped in an optical tweezer potential. The key mechanism exploited is the intrinsic Kerr nonlinearity arising from the anharmonicity of the Gaussian trapping potential, which allows for cat-state generation without external nonlinear elements.
key_observables: State fidelity ($F$), Cat size ($\alpha$), momentum quadratures ($\langle	ilde{p}angle/p_0$), and tunable Kerr nonlinearity coefficients ($c_2, c_4, c_6$).
important_parameters: Trap frequency ($\omega$), anharmonicity parameter ($\eta$), modulation amplitudes ($\epsilon_q, \epsilon_l$), and evolution time ($t_e$).
main_assumptions: The dynamics are assumed to remain effectively one-dimensional when modulating along a single axis (the $x$-dimension).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the process of cat state generation via adiabatic passage, show the dependence of observables on painting amplitude ($\kappa$), and detail TOF tomography setups.
paper_structure: The paper details the theoretical framework using an effective Hamiltonian incorporating Kerr nonlinearity, presents experimental protocols for preparing even/odd parity cat states through controlled modulation, and validates results using high-fidelity state characterization via TOF measurements.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses non-Gaussian quantum state engineering in a leading platform (optical tweezers), providing robust methods for generating resources relevant to quantum error correction codes and enhanced sensing.
